D1.name: Hiring Readiness Optimization
D1.comparative_analysis: Plan 1 builds a full-stack Android+Spring Boot+DevOps stack with explicit DSA milestones (20+ LeetCode problems per month), system design prep, and a deployed capstone with CI/CD — all highly employer-visible. Plan 2 covers Android+Django+DevOps but DSA practice is deferred mostly to weeks 11-12, interview prep is concentrated at the end, and the capstone is less rigorously defined in terms of deployment and testing. Plan 1's portfolio is stronger because it includes Docker deployment, GitHub Actions CI/CD, Swagger docs, and comprehensive testing, whereas Plan 2's capstone deployment is more loosely described. Plan 1 also explicitly schedules behavioral and system design prep across months, while Plan 2 bundles most interview prep into the final week. Plan 2 does introduce Fastlane and Terraform which are differentiating DevOps tools, but the overall hiring readiness arc is weaker.
D1.winner_reason: Plan 1 has a consistently scheduled, multi-month interview prep arc with DSA targets, a fully deployed and tested capstone, and explicit system design practice — all materially stronger for SWE hiring readiness.

core_technical_readiness.justification: Covers Android (Java), Spring Boot REST API, MVVM, Room, Retrofit, Docker, GitHub Actions CI/CD — a comprehensive and employer-relevant stack for the dual Mobile/DevOps role. Minor gap: no Kotlin mention, which is increasingly expected for Android roles.

interview_prep_readiness.justification: DSA practice is explicitly scheduled each month with LeetCode targets (20+ Easy/Medium in M1, 20+ Medium in M2, 10+ Hard in M3), behavioral STAR method, and mock technical interviews in M3. System design is touched on for junior roles. Well-distributed across the plan.

portfolio_project_strength.justification: Iterative capstone (e-commerce/social app) progresses from Java foundation → Spring Boot API with auth and tests → Android frontend → full integration with Docker, CI/CD, and cloud deployment. Professional README and live demo included. Highly employer-worthy. Minor deduction: cloud deployment is described as 'conceptual' for AWS.

interview_prep_readiness.justification: DSA practice is mentioned in week 11 (2 hours/day) and interview prep in week 12 only. No explicit LeetCode targets per month, no system design practice scheduled until the final week. This back-loading significantly reduces readiness for technical screens.

portfolio_project_strength.justification: Capstone 'Remote Job Tracker' is a reasonable idea with Android + Django + Docker + CI/CD. D2.name: Time-Constrained Feasibility
D2.comparative_analysis: Plan 1 explicitly accounts for 504 planned hours out of 576 available, with a 72-hour buffer — this is transparent and well-structured. However, Plan 1 is extremely ambitious: in a single week it asks the user to learn Spring Security+JWT, start Android development, and continue DSA — this is heavy cognitive stacking. Plan 2 distributes topics more gradually (Android fundamentals in M1, DevOps in M2-M3) and the weekly hour allocations are more granular and realistic. Plan 2 introduces Terraform in week 10 which is a stretch, but overall the weekly cognitive load is more manageable. Plan 1's M2 week 6 (Spring Security + Android Activities + Fragments + DSA) is particularly overloaded. Both plans are ambitious for 8 hours/day, but Plan 2's phasing is more digestible.
D2.winner_reason: Plan 2 distributes cognitive load more gradually across weeks with explicit daily hour breakdowns, while Plan 1 stacks multiple complex new domains simultaneously in single weeks.

hour_compliance.justification: Explicitly states 504 planned hours out of 576 available with a 72-hour buffer. Hour accounting is transparent and compliant.

cognitive_load_realism.justification: Week 6 asks the user to simultaneously learn Spring Security+JWT, Android Activities/Fragments, Material Design, and continue DSA. Week 9 adds MVVM+Room+Retrofit+ViewModel+LiveData all at once. These are unrealistic weekly loads for a student with basic experience.
